## Closing evidence — all 7 ACs re-measured on the LANDED tree

Change **3168** merged as `5cd7e2784ab` (`LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, 0 unresolved).

**The merged commit is not my commit, and the trees are not equal — that is expected and checked.**
My commit `e607f54110d` was based on `48c913d93d9`; Gerrit rebased it onto `403719c01ce`
(db2c's shim deletion) on submit. So the *trees* differ (`241a468f5eae` vs `48bf137c4564`)
while the *change* is identical: `git diff 48c913d93d9 e607f54110d` and
`git diff 403719c01ce 5cd7e2784ab` are **byte-identical, 586 lines each**. Tree-SHA equality
would have been the wrong check here and would have raised a false alarm.

The 9-check harness was then re-run with the worktree reset to `5cd7e2784ab`:

| Check | AC | Result |
|---|---|---|
| dead symbols absent from `src tests docs` (fixtures excluded) | AC1 | PASS |
| unresolvable-ref message single-sourced (exactly 1) | AC2 | PASS |
| schema verdict enum aligned with the wire | AC3 | PASS |
| `attest_gate` pass-through RETAINED | AC4 | PASS |
| `gate_runs.py` keeps its one `not-closed` (exactly 1) | AC5 | PASS |
| the two new tests green — 42 passed | AC6a | PASS |
| `test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py` passes UNMODIFIED — 40 passed | AC6b | PASS |
| `gen_types --check` clean | AC7a | PASS |
| `make verify` exit 0 — 20100 passed, 27 skipped, 48 warnings, 3544.89s | AC7b | PASS |

`RESULT pass=9 fail=0`.

### Two honest qualifications on that table

**AC7b reads a RECORDED run, not a fresh one.** The `make verify` it reports was executed
against `e607f54110d`, before the rebase. It is not a measurement of `5cd7e2784ab`. What
covers the gap is Gerrit CI's `Verified +1`, which ran on the submitted revision itself, plus
the byte-identical diff above and the fact that the only base movement was one
already-`Verified +1` commit. Re-running a 59-minute verify to re-derive a result CI had
already produced on the exact revision would not have added information.

**The AC7b check was broken when first written, and silently so.** It read
`nbad=$(grep -cE 'FAILED|ERROR' … || echo 0)`. `grep -c` **prints `0` and exits 1** on
no-match, so the `||` fired on success and the variable became the two-line string `"0\n0"`,
which `[ "$nbad" = "0" ]` can never match. The check could only ever report failure. Fixed to
`nbad=$(grep -cE … 2>/dev/null); nbad=${nbad:-0}`.

Before trusting the repaired harness I ran it against two negative controls: 19ba's recorded
4-failure log, and `/dev/null`. Both correctly FAILed, so the check has teeth rather than
merely having stopped complaining.

### One threshold worth flagging for whoever edits this next
AC7b asserts the suite is `>20000` tests. The real count is **20,100**, so the margin is 100.
(`AGENTS.md`'s "~19.2k tests" is stale.) A future change that deletes a meaningful number of
tests will trip this threshold for the wrong reason.

Closing. The work is on `main`.
